summary: Initial migration discovery: Citrine Cloud is exploring moving inference away from a mix of OpenAI hosted APIs + on-prem vLLM/TGI for cost and control. Key concerns are eval parity, latency at p95, data residency (EU), KMS integration, and SOC2/ISO artifacts. AE + SE explained Redwood hosted, Dedicated and Private options and high-level fallback/routing strategies. Agreed next steps include running a short parity benchmark and exchanging prompts and security docs.
topics: current stack, drivers for migration, hosting options (hosted/dedicated/private), benchmarking and eval parity, security/compliance, pricing and pilot scope
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-01-09 16:00 UTC | Duration 52m | Recorder: Fireflies.ai

Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood Solutions), Jordan (CTO, Citrine), Aisha (ML Eng), Samir (Security), Tess (PM)

00:00:05 Maya: ok everyone can hear me? testing audio
00:00:11 Jordan: yep good loud and clear, thanks for setting this up Maya, we've been looking forward to this call.
00:00:18 Maya: awesome, quick agenda — learn about your current infra, drivers to move, run through hosting options, align on next steps. Diego will take deep tech questions. sound good?
00:00:29 Jordan: sounds great. high level we run Citrine inference pipeline for our summarization and search augmentation. currently using a mix — for rapid prod features we route to OpenAI GPT endpoints, for cost sensitive heavy-batch we run vLLM on our GCP GPUs with Triton/TGI wrappers.
00:00:47 Aisha: yes and to add, the vLLM stack we built is kinda bespoke, TGI wrappers for a couple open models. it's working but ops cost is increasing and we need SLA for our paying customers, also EU data residency is a hard req for one of our customers.
00:01:03 Diego: okay got it — so hybrid today, OpenAI for latency & features, vLLM/TGI for batch and cost. what are your pain points most critical?
00:01:12 Aisha: the two big ones: 1) eval parity — model outputs aren't identical across runtimes and that creates downstream drift in our QA metrics; 2) ops overhead, especially handling peak bursts, and needing predictable p95 latency.
00:01:26 Tess: and procurement is pushing timeline — they'd like an MLP by H1 if we pick a vendor.
00:01:33 Maya: good, thanks — quick Redwood overview: we offer Hosted (fast api), Dedicated reserved pools for throughput guarantees, and Private (VPC / on-prem) for strict compliance. We also do smart routing so you can fall back between variants.
00:01:47 Jordan: couple questions — 1) if we move from OpenAI, how do you handle function calling and chat-style prompts? 2) Does Redwood ensure model/eval parity with our existing vLLM/TGI outputs?
00:02:02 Diego: on function calling — Redwood supports structured tool calls and streaming. For parity it's a two part story: inference engine will run the same model binary where possible, but kernel/quantization differences and tokenizer mismatches can cause drift. we do a parity program — we can run the same model weights and compare outputs, and also advise quantization and prompt-normalization to reduce drift.
00:02:26 Aisha: hmm tokenizer mismatch has bitten us. we use some custom preprocessing and control tokens. can we bring those?
00:02:33 Diego: yes you can bring tokenizer artifacts and we can wire them into the runtime. for private deployments you get full control. in hosted we support uploading tokenizer overrides and pre-/post-processing hooks via the client layer.
00:02:48 Samir: security question — KMS: we use HashiCorp Vault in our EU region, and some keys are HSM-backed. does Redwood integrate with customer-managed KMS/HSM?
00:02:58 Maya: short answer yes for Private we integrate with customer KMS/HSM and for Dedicated we have connectors to common KMS providers; for Hosted we offer envelope encryption and customer-managed keys via partner KMS in select regions — we'll share the exact integration matrix.
00:03:12 Samir: okay please share SOC2 and pen-test artifacts.
00:03:16 Priya: absolutely — we'll drop our SOC2 and ISO summaries and the security pack after the call.
00:03:23 Jordan: what about latency — our p95 for critical endpoints needs to be sub 280ms for short prompt generations (<=128 tokens) and p99 for larger ones 900-1.2s. can Redwood hit that?
00:03:38 Diego: depends on hosting choice and model. On dedicated pools with GPU selection tuned and our continuous batching disabled for low-latency routes we see p95 under 200ms on smaller models. For larger models p95 will be higher of course. we can run tests with your 3 canonical prompts to validate.
00:03:55 Aisha: great, we will provide prompts. another concern: throughput scaling during spikes — we get unpredictable bursts from SSO events or traffic spikes. how does autoscaling work?
00:04:06 Maya: Dedicated has reserved baseline capacity and burst policies; autoscaling is configurable with warm pools. private on-prem supports predefined node pools and autoscale hooks. fallback routing also lets you route less-critical traffic to cheaper variants in moments of contention.
00:04:22 Tess: cost: compared to OpenAI we need a 40-60% reduction on per-token unit cost to make this worthwhile given our margin targets. is that realistic?
00:04:32 Diego: often yes once you move heavy-batch to ded/priv and enable quantization + KV caching you can get big wins. Redwood Optimize recommends batching and quant settings per workload to hit those savings — Diego: we'll model your traffic and show run-rate TCO.
00:04:48 Jordan: curious about dev experience — we have 10+ engineers using OpenAI SDKs. what's the effort to switch?
00:04:56 Maya: we have drop-in SDK compatibility and quickstart templates. hosted mode is the lowest friction — single API key. Dedicated/Private will need some infra changes but we provide migration playbooks.
00:05:07 Aisha: on the parity tests — we run vLLM locally with LoRA adapters for some of our models. can Redwood run with the same LoRA + weight config?
00:05:16 Diego: yes, we can load LoRA adapters and run the same checkpoints; if there are custom TGI operator patches that's where we might see differences — we'll capture operator parity in the benchmark.
00:05:29 Jordan: let's talk timeline — if we sign a dedicated pilot in February can we go live by May?
00:05:36 Maya: typical pilot 4-8 weeks for eval + integration, production rollouts vary. May is plausible if we move quickly with prompts and security review.
00:05:45 Samir: compliance nitty gritty — we need audit logs, per-token metadata retention controls, SSO with SCIM and SAML enforced, and legal terms about data retention. Does Redwood provide per-customer audit logs and retention TTLs?
00:05:59 Priya: yes, audit logs are available with retention tiers. Private gives you the most control, Dedicated has log export and SSO options. We'll provide the retention matrix and SAML/SCIM docs.
00:06:13 Tess: procurement will ask about exit plan — we need clean portability. what does unlocking look like if we leave Redwood?
00:06:20 Diego: we provide model artifacts you supply, and we'll export usage logs and config. For private deployments you keep infrastructure; for dedicated/hosted we have a documented exit-runbook to export configs and traces. we'll work through hands-on steps during the pilot.
00:06:36 Jordan: good. quickly, any known gotchas moving from TGI -> Redwood?
00:06:41 Diego: TGI operator differences and custom kernels often cause output variation; quantization profiles can change tokens per prompt due to rounding. We mitigate by running the same weight binaries, aligning tokenizers, and running golden prompts to detect regressions.
00:06:56 Aisha: speaking of quantization, what's your default quant pipeline? we use 4-bit Q4 variants for cost.
00:07:03 Diego: we support multiple quant paths (Q8/Q4 variants) and recommend per-model testing. Redwood Optimize will suggest a quant profile per workload and we can A/B traffic to validate quality.
00:07:15 Jordan: ok let's move to concrete: what do you need from us to start the parity benchmark?
00:07:20 Maya: three things: 1) canonical prompt set (Aisha will send), 2) sample payload distribution (peak, p50/p95 token lengths), 3) model checkpoints or model names you're using (weights if possible).
00:07:33 Aisha: we'll provide prompts and a traffic CSV. note: some models are fine-tuned privately and under NDA — we may need to run tests in Private or via secure transfer.
00:07:44 Samir: confirm — does Redwood support per-customer isolation for private models under NDA?
00:07:49 Priya: yes, Private supports air-gapped or customer VPC deployments and encrypted images; we can do on-prem if needed.
00:07:57 Tess: one last thing — there's internal politics: platform team prefers Hosted for reduced ops, security prefers Private. we'd like a phased approach. can Redwood support hybrid?
00:08:08 Maya: absolutely — hybrid routing is a core pattern. start with Hosted for speed, Dedicated for predictable load, and Private for the regulated customer workload.
00:08:17 Jordan: excellent. can we also see a cost model comparing Hosted vs Dedicated for our 3-month run-rate?
00:08:24 Maya: yes we'll include that in the pricing sheet. Diego will run the parity bench and include cost sensitivity runs.
00:08:31 Diego: quick note — for the bench we'll run: openai baseline (if you can share request logs), vLLM/TGI internal baseline, Redwood hosted and Redwood Dedicated with same model/quant; we'll compare token output diffs, latency p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1M tokens.
00:08:48 Aisha: we may not be able to share OpenAI logs but we can share aggregated latencies and example request ids.
00:08:55 Maya: that's fine — aggregated stats and example prompts are enough for parity testing.
00:09:00 Jordan: anything else?
00:09:02 Maya: security deep-dive — we'll set that as a separate meeting and include our security lead. propose next Wed 1500 UTC.
00:09:09 Samir: works for me.
00:09:11 Tess: works for me.
00:09:13 Maya: great. recap of action items: Maya to send pricing and SOC2 doc, Diego to kick off parity bench once we get prompts, Aisha to send prompts and traffic profile, Samir to list compliance artifacts.
00:09:26 Jordan: thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity.
00:09:29 Maya: thanks all. end of recording.
